value: (1) 'Its own files' means the .py files in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/ that the runner imports (__main__.py, heartbeat.py, guard.py, liveness.py, discovery.py). A change to cairn/tools/base does not restart the loop. After the rewrite the runner imports only address.py from base, so this holds by construction. (2) Restart is os.execv of the same interpreter with the same module. The flock fd is O_CLOEXEC (PEP 446), so the claim drops at exec and the new image re-claims. If another starter wins that race, the new image exits 3 and the winner runs; that is the singleton contract, not a defect. (3) 'Running and ok' = the flock is held AND read_liveness says LIVE (record younger than STALENESS_THRESHOLD_S=300s). A lock holder whose record is DEAD is hung: the newcomer SIGTERMs the recorded pid and re-claims. That is the not-ok branch Akien's sentence implies. (4) A pulse.py exposes on_pulse(now, context) -> dict. Both existing sites (codemother, counting_block) have that shape. A module is loaded once and re-loaded when its mtime changes, because pulse modules keep module-level state (codemother's _last_head).
